title: Evaluation Runtime: Bounded Reliability Semantics
oneLiner: A small single-process evaluation runtime that makes execution attempts, ambiguous failures, and report denominators separately inspectable, under a machine-readable reliability contract.
keyTakeaways: Logical task identity and execution-attempt identity are separate durable concepts; retries append new history rather than overwrite prior attempts.

A crash between dispatching external work and committing its outcome projects as ambiguous_external_execution, and automatic recovery refuses to re-invoke the provider (fail closed) unless durable evidence proves a retryable failure.
Evaluations bind (run_id, evaluator_version) and judge only the execution-time expected_snapshot, never the mutable current task definition.
Report signals carry explicit denominators; undefined ratios are null rather than 0.0, and referentially invalid records are quarantined instead of averaged in.
hciRelevance: Adjacent to trust calibration: an AI system's reliability story is only inspectable if its execution history, failure ambiguity, and report denominators are visible rather than collapsed into one number.

faq.q: Does this runtime connect to a real LLM or provider?
faq.a: No. The agent is a deterministic mock plus deterministic fault injection. There is no network call, no provider integration, and no empirical validation of real-provider reliability.
No. It is single-process and single-writer; history is append plus userspace flush, which is not fsync, transactional, locked, or power-loss durable. There is no database, queue, or web service.

No (RC-14: NOT_SUPPORTED). It preserves uncertainty about whether an outcome-unknown invocation executed externally and blocks automatic replay; it cannot prove either way without a reconciliation mechanism it does not have.

faq.q: Is this a benchmark of model quality?
faq.a: No. It is evaluation-engineering evidence: how attempts, failures, judgments, and denominators are recorded and bounded. Its success criterion is that the agent returned a value, not that the output is valid.
Not yet. A fresh-root public snapshot has been prepared locally; publication is a separate owner decision. No public repository URL exists for it yet.
